label: Systems / environment dimension (global)
description: Superordinate node: the person as an autonomous unity embedded in a hierarchy of nested, mutually coupled environmental systems that supply and thwart the conditions of psychological functioning

label: Microsystem
description: Immediate face-to-face settings that contain the developing person and in which proximal processes occur (home, school, workplace, peer group)

label: Mesosystem
description: The system of microsystems: the interrelations among the immediate settings a person participates in (home-school, work-family linkages)

label: Exosystem
description: Settings that do not contain the person but impinge on the settings that do (caregiver workplace, local government, media, service systems, social networks)

label: Macrosystem
description: The overarching economic, political, legal, and cultural blueprints of a society, carried as institutions and as ideology, that pattern all lower systems

label: Chronosystem
description: The temporal dimension of the environment: ecological transitions, life-course change, cohort and historical time

label: Person-environment boundary (autopoietic interface)
description: The organizationally closed boundary of the person as a self-producing (autopoietic) unity that is structurally coupled to, but not determined by, its environment

label: Family / household
description: The primary microsystem: patterns of interaction among household members; the setting whose homeostasis and interaction sequences most strongly shape functioning
primary_source: Selvini Palazzoli et al. (1980); Szapocznik et al. (2012)

label: School / workplace
description: The achievement microsystem: educational or occupational setting with its roles, demands, and reinforcement structures

label: Peer / community group
description: The affiliative microsystem: peers, neighbourhood, and community networks that provide support, norms, and social capital

label: Cross-setting linkages
description: The connective tissue of the mesosystem: congruence or conflict between settings (e.g., home-school communication) that amplifies or buffers their separate effects

label: Caregiver economy / employment
description: The exosystem of parental or caregiver work and material resources whose stresses propagate into the microsystem as second-order effects

label: Service & health systems
description: The organized care system: mental-health, health, education, and social services, their coverage, quality, and accessibility

label: Media / information environment
description: The communicative exosystem: mass and digital media that transmit macro-level ideology and norms into settings

label: Local institutions / governance
description: Local agencies of government and civil society that administer resources and services at the concrete community level

label: State / government / law & policy
description: The political-legal macrosystem: the state's police and parens patriae powers, and the policies through which it shapes inequality, privacy, and access to care

label: Economic system / material resources
description: The macro-economic structure that determines the distribution of income, wealth, and material security across the population

label: Socioeconomic inequality
description: The gradient of socioeconomic position and its concentration; a macro-structural condition that patterns exposure to adversity

label: Cultural norms / ideology
description: Shared values, beliefs, and cognitive maps that give meaning and priority to settings, roles, and behaviours; reproduced across generations

label: Feedback / circular causality
description: Mechanism: circular, recursive causation and homeostatic regulation by which systems maintain steady states and resist change
primary_source: Wiener (in Lalande, 2011); Selvini Palazzoli et al. (1980)

label: Structural coupling
description: Mechanism: the recurrent person-environment interactions through which an autopoietic unity and its medium reciprocally trigger structural change without loss of autonomy

label: Proximal processes
description: Mechanism: the enduring, reciprocal, progressively more complex interactions in the microsystem that are the proximate engines of development

label: Social-determinant transduction
description: Mechanism: the pathways (scarcity, cognitive load, food insecurity, chronic stress) that convert macro-structural conditions into individual cognition and mental health
primary_source: Mani et al. (2013); Nagpaul et al. (2021); Liu & Li (2023)

label: Leverage points / systemic intervention
description: Mechanism: places in the system where a small, well-placed change produces large, distributed effects; the target of systemic therapy and systems-level policy

label: Person-model interface
description: Coupling node: the mother node of the person to which every systems influence is delivered and from which behaviour is emitted back into the environment

label: Needs interface (Batch F)
description: Coupling to the needs stratum: the environment as the field that satisfies or frustrates existence, safety, relatedness, and the other needs

label: Motivation-emotion / situation interface (Batch G)
description: Coupling to the motivation-emotion stratum: the situation as the appraised stimulus field feeding the valuation core
primary_source: Shah et al. (2018); Mani et al. (2013)

label: Development interface (Batch C)
description: Coupling to the developmental stratum: ecological transitions and proximal processes as the drivers and gates of development over time

label: Psychopathology interface (Batch A)
description: Coupling to the disorder stratum: systemic and social-determinant conditions as an environmental class of disorder priors

label: Therapy interface (Batch B)
description: Coupling to the therapy stratum: the systemic therapies and systems-level interventions that act on the environment as the treatment lever
primary_source: Retzlaff et al. (2013); Szapocznik et al. (2012)
